thread.title: Arrests Made in Child Exploitation Network 764
thread.title_full: Arrests Made in Child Exploitation Network 764

author: Rachel Acenas
title: Arrests Made in Child Exploitation Network 764
text:
• Two leaders of a child exploitation network known as 764 have been arrested.
• Prasan Nepal, 20, was arrested on April 22 in High Point, North Carolina.
• Leonidas Varagiannis, 21, was arrested on April 29 in Greece on an international warrant.
• Both defendants face charges of operating an international child exploitation enterprise.
• FBI Director Kash Patel described the operation as targeting innocent children.
• Varagiannis has denied the allegations and opposed extradition in court.
• His lawyer stated that Greek law and courts have jurisdiction over the case.
• Federal prosecutors allege the two men targeted children as young as 13 from late 2020 through early 2025.
• The network used threats, blackmail, and manipulation to coerce victims into producing explicit content.
• The FBI reported that the material was used to force victims into acts of violence and self-harm.
• The network also engaged in swatting and harassment to silence victims.
• A criminal complaint unsealed in the District of Columbia showed online manuals used by the defendants.
• The manuals instructed others on how to groom and extort minors.
• The case is part of Project Safe Childhood, launched by the DOJ in May 2006.
• The initiative aims to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse using federal, state, and local resources.
• Attorney General Pam Bondi called for swift justice in the case.
• If convicted, both defendants face a maximum penalty of life in prison.
